rules.summary: BP-EUR is core class P (the 'B' prefix means accumulating). Core class P is available to all investors, and the management company sets no requirements for it.

citations.quote: P All investors. Yes None None
For all other classes, shares that DO contain the prefix “B” are accumulation shares.

rules.summary: BI-EUR is core class I (accumulating), which is reserved for institutional investors. The prospectus defines institutional investors by reference to article 174 of the 2010 Law. They include credit institutions and other financial professionals investing for themselves or for other investors, including retail clients under a discretionary management agreement, as well as insurance companies, pension funds and other UCIs.

citations.quote: Institutional investors. Yes None

institutional investors Investors within the meaning of article 174 of the 2010 Law, such as credit institutions and other financial professionals investing on the behalf of themselves or other investors (whether retail in connection with a discretionary management agreement or institutional), as well as insurance companies, pension funds, or other UCIs.

rules.summary: Unless the board or the management company decides otherwise, US persons may not subscribe, and shares may not be offered or sold in the USA. The definition of US person is mixed: it is a list modelled on Regulation S (residency or place of organisation, ending with a catch-all for Rule 902 of Regulation S), with a carve-out for 'Non-United States persons' under CFTC Rule 4.7. US citizenship or US taxpayer status alone does not exclude: US taxpayers may subscribe as long as they are not US persons.

citations.quote: The shares in the SICAV may not be directly or indirectly offered or sold in the USA. Unless otherwise decided by the board or the management company, US persons may not subscribe for shares in the SICAV.
Therefore, US taxpayers, as defined for US federal income tax purposes, may subscribe for shares in the SICAV as long as they do not qualify as US persons.
any other U.S. person defined by US Rule 902 of Regulation S

rules.summary: Knowledge and experience is basic. The fund is for all investor types who understand its risks, and who accept that its value follows the underlying investments and can fluctuate. No advanced knowledge or experience is required. This value is inferred; the documents do not use an explicit knowledge label.

citations.quote: Investor profile Investors who understand the risks of the fund and plan to invest for at least 5 years.

The fund is intended for investors who accept and understand that the value of the fund is directly linked to the value of underlying investments, will fluctuate over time and that the invested amount can be lost entirely.

rules.summary: Shares may be offered or bought only where they are registered for public sale or where local law does not prohibit the sale. Some share classes may not be available in certain jurisdictions. The client's country of residence and the class's registration status must be checked.

rules.summary: The SICAV may reject any subscription in whole or in part. It may also soft-close (to new investors) or hard-close (to all further investment) a fund or share class without notice. The board decides eligibility requirements and ownership restrictions, and may compulsorily redeem shares held by ineligible holders.

citations.quote: A closure may apply only to new investors (soft closure) or to further investments from existing shareholders as well (hard closure).
